body.text: A day on the princes islands istanbul archipelago feels worlds away from mainland traffic, yet sits inside Istanbul's municipal ferry network. Once summer retreats for Ottoman elites and Greek, Armenian, and Jewish Istanbulites, the four main inhabited islands—Kınalıada, Burgazada, Heybeliada, and Büyükada—reward travelers who choose the right island and avoid Sunday ferry bottlenecks.
How do you reach Büyükada by ferry?

Board official Şehir Hatları municipal ferries from Kabataş (European side) or Bostancı (Asian side) using an Istanbulkart. In 2026, a full-fare Islands crossing costs 151.23 TL. Kabataş boats stop at Kadıköy and the smaller islands, taking about 1 hour 45 minutes to Büyükada; Bostancı boats reach Büyükada in 35 to 45 minutes.

Check seasonal departures on the [Şehir Hatları Kabataş–Adalar timetable](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips/adalar-princes-islands-lines/kabatas-adalar-177) or the [Bostancı–Adalar circuit schedule](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips/adalar-princes-islands-lines/bostanci-adalar-circuit-line-770), as winter and summer frequencies differ. Beşiktaş also runs direct seasonal sailings ([Şehir Hatları Adalar–Beşiktaş](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips/adalar-princes-islands-lines/adalar-besiktas-769)). Private motor operators like Mavi Marmara run parallel routes, though municipal Şehir Hatları boats offer larger open decks and steadier rides in Marmara chop. Top up your card before reaching the pier using our [Istanbul public transport guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/istanbul-public-transport-guide).
Which island is quieter — Büyükada, Heybeliada or Burgazada?

Burgazada is the quietest of the three, followed by pine-forested Heybeliada, while Büyükada is the largest, grandest, and busiest. Choose Büyükada for historic timber mansions and the hilltop Aya Yorgi monastery, Heybeliada for leafy walks and the historic Halki Seminary, and Burgazada for unhurried seaside lunches and literary history.

items: Büyükada: Home to the 202-meter Yüce Tepe climb up to [Aya Yorgi Church](https://istanbul-tourist-information.com/hagios-georgios-church-aya-yorgi/) and ornate late-Ottoman wooden villas along Nizam Caddesi. Crowds cluster near the clock-tower pier; walking twenty minutes past the harbor clears the noise.
Heybeliada: Anchored by the 1844 [Halki Seminary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halki_seminary) atop Hope Hill and shaded coastal pine loops with fewer day-trip groups.

Burgazada: Compact and fiercely local, featuring the free [Sait Faik Abasıyanık Museum](https://saitfaikmuzesi.org/iletisim/) (open Wednesday–Sunday, 10:30–16:45; closed Monday–Tuesday) and sunset views from Kalpazankaya.

body.text: How do you get around without cars?

Private motor vehicles are strictly prohibited on the Princes' Islands, and Istanbul permanently abolished horse-drawn carriages (fayton) in 2020. Today visitors explore the pine-lined hills on foot, rent bicycles near the main piers, or ride İETT's quiet electric minibuses (Adabüs) using a standard Istanbulkart.

[İETT's Adalar electric transit](https://iett.istanbul/icerik/adalara-ulasim) runs loop routes across Büyükada, Heybeliada, and Burgazada, including the uphill stretch toward Büyükada's Luna Park square (where the final steep footpath to Aya Yorgi begins). Check current island shuttle tariffs on the [İETT Adalar fare page](https://iett.istanbul/icerik/Adalar-ucret-Tarifesi). If renting a bicycle on Büyükada, test the brakes before leaving the shop—several back hills are steep and cobbled.
Which months are best to avoid weekend crowds?

Visit in April, May, September, or October—and specifically on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday—for warm walking weather without shoulder-to-shoulder ferry queues. Avoid July and August weekends, national holidays, and April 23 (St. George's Day), when tens of thousands pack Büyükada's hilltop paths.

Spring brings wisteria and mimosa across the wooden mansion gardens, while September and October keep the Sea of Marmara warm enough for late-season swims on Heybeliada and Burgazada. Winter weekdays are wonderfully peaceful for tea and architecture walks, though several seasonal beach clubs close and wind can cancel smaller private boats. Pair an early return ferry with dinner on the Asian side or Karaköy using our [Istanbul food guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/istanbul-food-guide).

faq.q: How much is the ferry to Büyükada in 2026?
faq.a: A full-fare one-way ticket on Şehir Hatları municipal ferries from Kabataş, Kadıköy, or Bostancı to the Princes' Islands costs 151.23 TL with an Istanbulkart in 2026 ([Şehir Hatları](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/price-list)).

faq.q: Can I visit both Heybeliada and Büyükada in one day?
faq.a: You can, since ferries hop between them in 15 minutes, but doing two islands usually turns the day into pier-waiting. Picking one island and walking its quieter back loop is far more enjoyable.

faq.q: Are horse carriages still operating on Büyükada?
faq.a: No. Istanbul abolished horse-drawn carriages on the Princes' Islands in 2020 for animal welfare reasons. Electric İETT minibuses now serve the island loops.

faq.q: Can you swim on the Princes' Islands?
faq.a: Yes, mostly from June through September at paid beach clubs or rocky coves on Heybeliada, Burgazada, and Büyükada's southern shore. Water shoes help on stony entries.

faq.q: How steep is the walk to Aya Yorgi Church on Büyükada?
faq.a: The final brick-paved climb from Luna Park square takes 15 to 20 minutes uphill and is steep. Take an İETT electric shuttle to Luna Park first to save energy for the summit.

faq.q: Do I need to book Princes' Islands ferry tickets in advance?
faq.a: No. Municipal Şehir Hatları ferries operate on a turnstile Istanbulkart system with no seat reservations. Arrive 15–20 minutes early on sunny days to claim an upper-deck bench.
